newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - STANBIC YR SHR SEEN UP 23-25 PCT.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - STANBIC YR SHR SEEN UP 23-25 PCT.

text.p: Standard Bank Investment Corp Ltd (Stanbic) would report earnings growth of between 23 and 25 percent for the year to December 31 1995, hoisted by associate Liberty Life Association of Africa Ltd , analysts said.

Interest margins were seen under pressure following the liquidity crunch in the money market last year -- which saw short-term interest rates soar -- but this would be offset by positive factors such as Liberty's contribution and good growth on the advances and instalment credit side.

Analysts polled forecast Stanbic's 1996 earnings would rise to between 13 rand and 13.05 rand a share from 10.53 rand at the 1995 year-end. They expected a dividend of between 390 and 405 cents compared with 327 cents a year ago.
Stanbic, South Africa's second largest banking group, owns 50 percent of Liblife Controlling Corp Ltd, which is the ultimate holding company of Liberty Life Asociation of Africa Ltd.
"The big kick will come from the Liberty Life unit," said one analyst who declined to be quoted.
Liberty Life reported a 58 percent increase in attributable earnings in the 1995 December year-end after adopting new disclosure standards for the first time for its results.

Margin wise, net interest income would not keep up with advances growth but this was expected to be balanced by reasonably strong growth on the non-interest revenue side because of the favourable impact of trading in the currency, the analyst said.
"The squeeze in the money market will have dented margins to some extent but I don't think enough to hold back growth," David Southey, an analyst at Edey Rogers said.
Another analyst also noted the group has been showing good growth instalment credit and on the general advances side.
Expenses were seen reasonably well controlled, leveraging the overall pre-tax numbers up by around 20 percent.
The bad debt line was not expected to be as hard hit for the full year compared to the interim stage.
Stanbic raised its bad and doubtful debt charge to 288 million rand in the six months to June 30, 1996, from 243 million rand in the comparative 1995 period.
Some analysts said they were looking for growth in associates of over 60 percent which should leave attributable income up by over 23 percent.

"The important thing to note is that the group has managed to smooth its earnings growth over a number of years...it has always managed to show growth somewhere in the region of 20 percent," Southey said.
But he noted that the interim stage in June 1997 could well see significantly lower earnings growth because of the comparison with the higher June base last year, buoyed by Liberty's performance.

Looking ahead, analysts said Stanbic -- as well as other leading banks -- would this year be faced with far slower advances growth and higher bad debt but there should be some relief in margins later in the year due to improved money market conditions.
But one noted that a declining credit extension trend could dampen the positive effects of the money market:
"It's a double edged sword...credit extension is coming down leading to a scenario where the pressure on margins could ease but assets are going to grow slower," the analyst said.
